correctness.rationale: A cover forces conjugate length-ell prefix and suffix, so their one-counts agree. Unequal flanks yield the exact lower threshold. Equal flanks yield a central run covered from its ends precisely when \(2r\ge b\). Unique occurrence of the one-run then yields the exact individual-factor census. Cyclic roots admit at most two conjugate blocks, with a two-block root precisely at even b and \(a=c\). The standalone direct enumerator passes 1,250 cases and 26,029 length tests; unrestricted correctness rests on the four-part proof.

evidence: CPM 2023 Theorem 22 provides a linear-time algorithm for the cyclic-cover problem on arbitrary strings; Definitions 1 and 10 treat cover and quasi-cover notions.
Grossi et al., WALCOM 2023 and the 2025-online journal revision present an algorithm for every input, with the singleton-middle-run example explicitly displayed.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These papers are algorithmically broader in the domain of input strings, and every finite instance of the present theorem is computable by their algorithms. However the examined mathematical statements give no uniform length-threshold or factor-count formula for \(0^a1^b0^c\) with \(b\ge2\), no outer-flank symmetry bifurcation and no one-letter instability theorem. The present result does not claim a stronger general algorithm.

value.rationale: This is the complete cyclic-cover and cyclic-root length spectrum, the all-length number of distinct covering factor strings, and their total count for all two-transition binary words with non-singleton middle run. It reveals a discontinuity of unbounded magnitude under one inserted zero and a b-independent covering-factor total for unequal flanks. The all-length structural counting law is not a textbook renaming or a finite known-table recomputation.
